beats.summary: Michael informs the office that Ed Truck, his former boss, has died.

evidence.snippet: Jan (on speakerphone): So, I wanted to let you know that we lost Ed Truck.
Michael: Attention, everybody. I just received a call from corporate with some news they felt that I should know first. My old boss Ed Truck has died.

beats.summary: Michael struggles with how to properly honor Ed Truck and clashes with Jan over the idea of giving the office a day off.

evidence.snippet: Michael: I don't understand. We have a day honoring Martin Luther King, but he didn't even work here.
Jan (on speakerphone): I understand how you feel, Michael. I really do. So, would it be helpful to give everyone the day off?

beats.summary: Creed describes Ed Truck's death as a decapitation in a drunken accident, leading to humorous exchanges about death and decapitation.

evidence.snippet: Creed: He was drunk as a skunk, he was flying down Route 6. He slides under an 18 wheeler. Pop. It snaps right off.

beats.summary: Michael humorously performs errands for coworkers by pretending to go to the warehouse and kitchen.

evidence.snippet: Michael: Hey Ryan, can I get you a pencil from the warehouse?

Michael (breathless): All right. Okay.
[STAGE] goes back down pretend stairs, crawls on belly to the kitchen for the coffee

beats.summary: Dwight expresses his wishes about his own death and cryogenic freezing to Angela.

evidence.snippet: Dwight: If my head ever comes off, I would like you to put it on ice.
Dwight: When I die, I wanna be frozen. And if they have to freeze me in pieces, so be it.

beats.summary: Jim and Karen engage in a lighthearted conflict over snack chips and project supervision.

evidence.snippet:

Michael: Hey Ryan, can I get you a pencil from the warehouse?
Ryan: Uh, no thanks, I'm good.
Michael: Oh, it's okay, I'm going down.
Ryan: Um… Yeah, absolutely.
Michael: All right, I'll be right back.
[STAGE] goes down pr
